beats.narration_text: The model calls a tool, you run it, feed the result back — and it calls again; something has to end the loop, but nothing in your code says when.

The runner peeks at each response for `tool_use` blocks; finding one, it executes and re-prompts; finding none, it stops. Termination is the model choosing not to call a tool — the loop is model-controlled.
beats.visual: A circular flow: message → response → check tool_use? → execute → re-prompt → loop or exit.
beats.scaffold_note: the resolving mechanism; orbits the visual object

beats.narration_text: "What is 9 + 10?" → model calls `sum(9,10)` → runner returns "19" → re-prompts → model replies "The answer is 19." with no tool call → loop exits.

The runner peeks at each response for `tool_use` blocks; finding one, it executes and re-prompts; finding none, it stops. Termination is the model choosing not to call a tool — the loop is model-controlled.

Your turn. Paste this: your tool-calling loop keeps going with tool_runner and you're not sure what makes it stop — is it your code or the model's decision? Ask Claude to show you the control flow — which condition triggers the model to stop producing tool_use blocks, what your code should check in each response to know whether to re-prompt or return, and give you the minimal correct implementation of the loop.
